why: Micronauts are programs capable of acting as agents, which does not prove that any particular Micronaut is one. Agency is a behavioural claim, so it is demonstrated operationally: generate a subgoal, choose an action from context rather than a template, invoke a capability through the authorized registry, observe the result and change the next decision, and emit a verified learning delta or an explicit no-change. Autonomy adds one test — a further bounded round initiated without a new user message.

classification.law: classification uses registry facts only — is it runnable, does it declare selectable capabilities — and never a claim inferred from a name
classification.program: runnable, declares no capabilities: it executes but takes no part in a selection loop
classification.agent_capable: runnable and declares capabilities: it can participate in observe → evaluate → select → act → feedback
classification.unrunnable: cannot act at all: unregistered, or registered with no driver manifest
classification.no_llm_required: agenthood does not require a model: this loop is rules and arithmetic over the registry, AIML-style subgoals and a bounded budget, and it is exactly reproducible

loop.subgoal: the next subgoal is the first planned capability not yet satisfied, so the goal drives the round rather than a fixed script
loop.selection: the action is chosen against current state; a capability that already failed is not preferred while an alternative remains, so observation changes the decision
loop.invocation: a capability resolves to a registered and runnable Micronaut through the registry; the executor receives the resolved Micronaut and never a bare capability name
loop.feedback: each round records success or failure and an observation, which becomes part of the state the next decision reads
loop.budget: the loop is bounded by the declared maximum rounds, and reaching it is reported as budget_exhausted rather than success
loop.authorization: XCXE authorizes capabilities, not the agent's intentions: a capability outside the grant is not executed, and the run reports blocked

autonomy.law: autonomy is not unlimited scope: it is the ability to run another bounded round under an existing authorization without a new user message
autonomy.prohibited: an autonomous round may not widen its authorization, invent a capability, or continue past the budget

learning.law: a run ends with a verified learning delta or an explicit no-change outcome, never with silence
learning.note: the delta goes through the LearningDelta contract, so a run that taught nothing reports NO_CHANGE rather than pretending otherwise

invariants.AG1: a Micronaut is classified from registry facts only, and the classification vocabulary is program, agent_capable, autonomous_coordinator, unrunnable
invariants.AG2: the loop generates or selects a relevant subgoal from the goal's plan rather than replaying a fixed script
invariants.AG3: the selected action depends on current state: after a failed attempt the next decision differs while an alternative remains
invariants.AG4: an action is invoked through the authorized registry, resolves to a registered and runnable Micronaut, and a capability outside the grant is not executed
invariants.AG5: the run observes its results and records them into the state the next decision reads
invariants.AG6: a run ends with a learning delta or an explicit NO_CHANGE outcome, and never with an unrecorded result
invariants.AG7: autonomy is bounded: a further round may run without a new prompt, but only within the authorized set and the declared round budget, and reaching the budget is reported as budget_exhausted
invariants.AG8: the loop is deterministic and model-free: the same goal, registry and authorization produce the same rounds, so agency is reproducible evidence rather than a description
